acceptanceResults: A separate activity_read_store view uses the configured existing repository connection and a single owner-correlated SELECT. The maximum session id chooses token and status from the same row, even when creation timestamps conflict.

Only the known lifecycle enum is serialized; no session, null/empty or unrecognized state becomes unknown. Failed, expired and unknown latest state have no token; an older active token cannot reappear.
Pending failed/expired sessions show closure/support advice and suppress even an injected legacy action token. No failed-funds, failed-order, refund or automatic retry claim is introduced.

Sent receipt keeps the review label, stored receipt gets the received-file label, and both retain receipt evidence plus closure advice. Paid/sent/terminal order states dominate old session closure metadata; delayed-paid and transaction evidence remain intact.
Unknown/missing session metadata never creates a closure claim. Existing legacy missing-field UI behavior remains compatible, while the new backend omits tokens for unknown state.

At 320,390,1280px actual refresh/filter controls render all closure/receipt variants, known nonclosed/unknown/missing states and nonpending order precedence; support is keyboard-usable and cards fit their width.
Inspected 320px cards show legible closure guidance and support with no payment action. The long no-receipt status and date wrap without overlap; receipt variants retain clear labels.
Legacy customer_orders and bot field projections remain unchanged. The actual retained installed dependency and disposable PostgreSQL17.11 both pass the new view contract.

independentEvidence.method: Actual legacy/new SQL and API serialization on :memory: data followed by exact old/new rendering; foreign owner excluded, one snapshot SELECT, no provider/runtime calls.
independentEvidence.methodOps: All runtime calls replaced by inert fixtures and mutation functions forbidden; observe interrupted deployment/rollback/terminal journals without replay.

operationalReview.scope: Add module, replace main/HTML, restart Relay once after binding all gates; existing order_read_store live digest preserved.
verifiedDesign: Local flock plus stopped-autopilot guard; exact original/candidate/recipe manifest and input-bound gates reject drift before publication.
Private fsynced preimages and ownership/mode/mtime/xattrs recorded before module-main-HTML publication; journal persists mutation/restart intent before action.
Interrupted deploy is observed without replay; explicit rollback accepts only known original/candidate bytes and exact preimages.
Rollback restores old main/HTML, restarts and verifies Relay before deleting the exact additive module. Bot/Nginx/PostgreSQL service identities are required to remain unchanged.
Runtime probes use only public GET/POST webapp and unauthenticated history403; no real customer identity or provider/payment request is sent.

correctedFinding.issue: Initial reconcile guidance recommended explicit rollback even for ROLLBACK_* journals, although rollback rejects those states.
correctedFinding.resolution: Guidance now requires independent inspection/manual completion for interrupted rollback while preserving no-blind-replay guards; five independent acceptance probes and author regression cover this.

operationalReview.preflight: PASS on exact live baseline, absent new module, active services, stopped autopilot and GET200/POST405/unauthenticated history403.
operationalReview.rehearsal: Seven atomic publication/restoration/journal observations pass; fourteen isolated operational tests cover interruption, drift, replay and rollback ordering.
operationalReview.limits: Production restart/rollback not rehearsed. If rollback itself is interrupted, independent inspection/manual completion is required; no automatic repeat is authorized. Restart resumes unchanged ordinary runtime workers.

verification.unchangedBrowserLimits: Default motion, existing 5000ms action/cleanup and 120s unit cap; no forced click or timeout relaxation.
verification.postgresIsolation: Pinned image, network none, no host ports, disposable Unix socket; container and temporary directory removed.

limitations: Product acceptance uses synthetic backend data and isolated Chrome; real Telegram/iOS/WebKit, screen readers and human comprehension remain unverified.
Session closure is distinct from order outcome and payment/chain confirmation. The implementation neither declares lost funds nor initiates a new payment.

Known pre-existing installed payment handler/read-method mismatch remains explicitly recorded for the next slice; this PASS covers the activity view and its bounded rollout, not the entire payment system.
The rollout requires a Relay restart, which resumes its existing cleanup/notification/provider workers. No claim of zero ordinary background effects is made.
Exact installed disk source and isolated handler behavior were reviewed; production-loaded object state and authenticated customer flows were not inspected.
Production replacement/runtime verification is primary-agent work. E4 and earlier gates remain open.
